thread:
sam: FYI I opened a docs PR with a compact on-prem "quick-fixes" section for air-gapped installs: focuses on (1) nftables ordering for host <-> pod traffic, (2) using socat as a troubleshooting bridge for unix-socket KMS proxies, and (3) a systemd drop-in that uses RequiresMountsFor to avoid race with offline bundles. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 (WIP).

nina: Nice. Can you paste the exact snippets so I can sanity-check wording and code blocks?

sam: sure. systemd drop-in we recommend:

```
# /etc/systemd/system/redwood-install.service.d/wait-offline.conf
[Unit]
Description=Ensure offline bundle mount before installer runs
RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/offline-bundle
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Environment=OFFLINE_BUNDLE_PATH=/mnt/offline-bundle
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/test -d $OFFLINE_BUNDLE_PATH
```

sam: For nftables ordering note (many customers use nft by default now):

```
# ensure host-forward rules applied before kube-proxy nat table
table ip filter {
    chain prerouting {
        type filter hook prerouting priority -150; policy accept;
        iifname "eth0" tcp dport 10250 counter accept
    }
}
# verify ordering with: sudo nft list ruleset | sed -n '1,120p'
```

evas: Good call calling out nft ordering. Can you add a troubleshooting command to show conntrack sizes?

sam: added: `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` plus `sudo nft list ruleset` for ordering.

nina: Socat bridge example please 1  (we had a support case where team needed TCP-only HSM vendor tools to hit a local unix socket).

sam: here's the one-liner we put in the doc as a debug helper:

```
# bridge unix socket -> tcp 127.0.0.1:8200 for vendor tooling
socat UNIX-LISTEN:/var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock,fork,mode=660 TCP-LISTEN:8200,reuseaddr
# test with: curl --unix-socket /var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock http://localhost/health
```

evas: Great. Make sure we warn not to run the bridge in production; only for local debugging. Also mention systemd socket-activated proxies if customers want persistent bridging.

sam: done. Added a small systemd socket unit example for permanent socket ownership: `redwood-kms.socket` + `redwood-kms.service` with `Socket` configured and `ListenStream=` pointing at the unix path.

nina: SDK snippet ask: can you include a tiny JS example that prefers env var token and falls back to unix socket config? Keep it tiny.

sam: added this JS snippet:```js
// prefer env token, then fall back to unix socket config
const REDWOOD_KMS_TOKEN = process.env.REDWOOD_KMS_TOKEN || null;
const config = {
  kmsSocket: process.env.KMS_SOCKET_PATH || '/var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock',
  authToken: REDWOOD_KMS_TOKEN
};
// SDK will try socket first when detected
```

evas: and a Go snippet? customers with infra teams love Go examples.

sam: small Go example added (env-first):```go
// env-first KMS config
token := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KMS_TOKEN")
socket := os.Getenv("KMS_SOCKET_PATH")
if socket == "" { socket = "/var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock" }
cfg := KMSConfig{SocketPath: socket, Token: token}
```

nina: style: avoid absolute assumptions about /usr/lib paths in HSM examples. Use a note: "verify vendor module path" and show command: `find / -name "libpkcs11*" 2>/dev/null`.

sam: good catch, updated. Also added a short HSM troubleshooting checklist: socket exists, perms, PKCS#11 module path, slot mapping, vendor logs, and `pkcs11-tool --module $MODULE -L`.
